# Generation recipe

All artwork was generated with the built-in image-generation tool, using the original Ash & Aether visual-development board and apprentice turnaround as references. Character variations used six requested expression states: neutral attentive, warm delighted smile, alarmed fearful, angry determined, sad vulnerable, and eyes closed resting.

Identity constraints: apprentice with warm brown skin, amber eyes, short tousled black hair, angular nose, teal work shirt and worn ochre apron; older mechanic with silver braid, strong brows, mature broad face, red scarf, cream work shirt and dark apron; asymmetric ivory ceramic creature with brass joints and cyan mechanical eyes. Preserve these identities, palette, proportions and materials across variants. Use crisp expressive ink contours, restrained cel shading and a theatrical fantasy-adventure illustration style. Portrait requests specified waist-up framing, one subject, no UI or text, and transparent backgrounds.

Background requests specified six standalone wide paintings matching the reference architecture and materials: sunset workshop, canal street at dawn, night workshop, twilight rooftops, apprentice bedroom and machine chamber. Requested no people, text or UI, readable entrances and paths, purposeful props and open foreground space. The resulting night workshop includes the creature as a fixed element; the canal street lighting reads as golden hour rather than a verified dawn.

Cleanup edits used each individual portrait as the only input and requested preservation of its face, expression, pose, costume and style while removing secondary characters and all backdrop glow. Some translucent matte remains despite this request. Check edges and matte against the intended shot background before final compositing.

Generation is not deterministic. These instructions document intent, not a guarantee that regenerating produces identical pixels. Use the delivered image assets as visual references for subsequent work.
